correctness.rationale: The complete nine-dimensional quotient has 511 nonzero sections. Exact four-chart Groebner unit-ideal criteria for the Jacobian minors classify 240 geometrically smooth sections. Every 2-dimensional \(\mathbf F_2\) subspace is represented uniquely by its sorted triple of nonzero masks. The checker exhausts all smooth pairs, giving 4,020 pencils, and enumerates all 120 automorphisms and all 36 orbits. Rank-three Jacobian tests decide base reducedness. A direct fifteen-plane-product argument proves that no smooth section contains all five rational points and hence no all-smooth pencil contains four rational base points. Explicit section masks (34,202,232) attain three; Groebner elimination gives an irreducible quintic residual orbit and verifies geometric reducedness. Full 36-orbit data and executable checks were replayed from the supplied paths before review.

originality.rationale: The accepted contribution is the combined exact all-smooth pencil census, orbit stratification, reducedness profile, and unique (1,1,1,5) extremal base type on the fixed nonsplit binary quadric. A five-point obstruction and the count of 240 individual smooth sections are not independently claimed novel. The inspected Asgarli–Ghioca papers instead treat hypersurface pencils and simultaneous transverse hyperplanes. General smooth quadric-surface pencil classifications and split-quadric computations do not logically determine this fixed-nonsplit-quadric genus-one pencil census. Unindexed equivalent finite computation remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The object is the intrinsic anticanonical pencil space on the unique nonsplit degree-eight del Pezzo form over \(\mathbf F_2\), and the base-locus incidence of genus-one smooth rational members is a natural geometric classification. In addition to a complete 4,020-pencils/36-orbits/reducedness census, the unique extremal 120-pencil orbit has a geometric Frobenius base-point type (1,1,1,5), a structural arithmetic invariant not given by individual curve counts. This distinguishes rational from geometric base-point behavior without asserting any unproved extension to other fields.
